title: Home beer dispenser
description: a home beer dispenser designed to dispense bottled beer using a hand-operated valve and compressed carbon dioxide
reference_excerpt: The product in question is a home beer dispenser, specifically designed for dispensing bottled beer. It operates using a hand-operated valve that introduces compressed carbon dioxide (CO2) into the beer bottle, pressurizing it to control the flow of beer. The dispenser is made from various plastic components. According to the Harmonized Tariff Schedule of the United States (HTSUS), the applicable subheading for this type of product falls under 8481.80.5090, which covers "other taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances, hand operated, of other materials." classification.rationale: The beer dispenser is itself a hand-operated tap/valve controlling the flow of beer under CO2 pressure, squarely within heading 8481's text for 'taps, cocks, valves and similar appliances.' Section XVI Note 1 excludes no such article, and Section XVI Note 2(a) confirms that an appliance which is itself a good of a chapter 84 heading (here 8481) is classified there directly rather than as a part of another machine, so the parts-suitability test in Note 2(b) is not the operative provision. HQ H250151, an in-force ruling, expressly confirms CBP's classification of a home beer dispenser with a hand-operated valve in subheading 8481.80.50, and the 'Other' statistical suffix applies because the article is neither a pressure spray can valve nor a bath/shower/sink/lavatory faucet.
